title: Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management: bring your own detections as custom indicators
summary: The briefing is held because it reports the default as unstated even though Microsoft documents disabled indicators and required administrator configuration for the preview. The roadmap details, configuration controls and published limits are supported; the policy path needs only a fuller route.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to accept customer user-activity indicators from homegrown systems, SIEM/UEBA platforms and line-of-business applications for existing Insider Risk Management playbooks.
claims.quote:
Allow customers to bring their own user activity
indicators from homegrown, SIEM/UEBA platforms, or other line-of-business
applications, and leverage them in existing Insider Risk Management playbooks.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents the Insider Risk Indicators connector as preview rather than a final general availability design.
claims.quote: Set up a connector to import third-party insider risk detections (preview)

claims.claim: The documented process requires creating a connector, creating custom indicators and using them in policies.
claims.quote: Bringing your own detections to insider risk management is a three-step process:

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Import accepts preprocessed, aggregated SIEM detections as files, not raw detection signals.
claims.quote: Currently, you can't import "raw" detection signals into insider risk management. You can only import preprocessed aggregations as a file.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Custom indicators can be used only with Data theft and Data leaks templates.
claims.quote: You can only use custom indicators with the Data theft and Data leaks templates.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: A custom trigger can bring a user into policy scope when activity crosses its configured threshold.
claims.quote: When user activity crosses the threshold value that you specify for the policy, the user is brought into scope of the insider risk management policy and is scored for risk.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Custom indicators can contribute to user risk scoring.
claims.quote: You can use a custom indicator as: A trigger to bring a user into the scope of a policy. A policy indicator to score the user for risk.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Learn describes an alert that analysts can investigate using custom indicator details.
claims.quote: An alert is generated and analysts can investigate the alert using custom indicator details.

claims.claim: The documented examples include a leaver-prediction trigger and Salesforce and Dropbox policy indicators.
claims.quote: Example 1 below shows how to prepare a CSV file for a 'home-grown' trigger that predicts the probability of an employee leaving an organization.

claims.claim: The receiving Insider Risk Management solution can lead from identified risks to investigation cases.
claims.quote: After identifying the risks, you can take action to mitigate these risks, and if necessary open investigation cases and take appropriate legal action.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/insider-risk-management-solution-overview to sources for the statement about investigation cases.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: The default is unknown and Microsoft has not stated what happens on arrival.
claims.quote: All global indicators are disabled by default; you must select one or more indicators to configure an Insider Risk Management policy.
claims.fix: Set defaultState to admin-opt-in for the documented preview. Replace the summary's default clause with 'The documented preview requires administrator configuration.' Replace the broad arrival statement in Why it matters with 'The preview requires an administrator to create the connector, custom indicator and policy; all global indicators are disabled by default.' Retain only the narrower open question about whether general availability will change this behaviour. The connector setup is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/import-insider-risk-indicators and the disabled default at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/insider-risk-management-settings-policy-indicators.

claims.claim: A CSV record requires the user's Microsoft Entra user principal name.
claims.quote: Only the UserPrincipalName and date/time fields are mandatory.

claims.claim: A CSV record requires the time the activity occurred.
claims.quote: Mandatory field that displays the date/time that the activity occurred.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Additional CSV fields are optional and appear in Activity explorer, alerts and cases.
claims.quote: All other fields are optional but can be helpful for the analyst or investigator in decision making when they triage alerts (these fields appear in the Activity explorer and in alerts and cases).

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The sample script uploads the CSV data to the Microsoft cloud.
claims.quote: The sample script that you run in Step 4 uploads your data to the Microsoft cloud so that the insider risk management solution can use it.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Cost and licensing: Indirect costs
claims.claim: A registered Microsoft Entra application authenticates the connector and upload script.
claims.quote: When you create this app, Microsoft Entra ID can authenticate the connector when it runs and attempts to access your organization. Use this app to authenticate the script that you run in Step 4

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The script takes the Microsoft Entra application secret as a parameter.
claims.quote: appSecret | This is the Microsoft Entra application secret for the app that you created in Microsoft Entra ID in Step 1. This value is also used for authentication.

claims.claim: The sample script is not supported under a Microsoft standard support program.
claims.quote: This sample script isn't supported under any Microsoft standard support program or service.

claims.claim: The script requires webhook.ingestion.office.com to be allowed through the organisation's firewall.
claims.quote: Make sure to add the webhook.ingestion.office.com domain to your firewall allowlist for your organization. If this domain is blocked, the script doesn't run.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft instructs administrators to use a custom threshold rather than default thresholds for selected custom triggers or indicators.
claims.quote: After selecting your custom trigger or indicator, make sure to set a custom threshold (don't use the default thresholds).

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Trigger thresholds cannot be set when Use only as a triggering event without any thresholds is selected.
claims.quote: You can't set trigger thresholds on a custom indicator if you select the Use only as a triggering event without any thresholds option.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The maximum number of custom indicators is 10.
claims.quote: Maximum number of custom indicators. | 10

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The maximum number of fields per custom indicator is 20.
claims.quote: Maximum number of fields per custom indicator. | 20

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Custom indicator triggers have a limit of 15,000 per UTC calendar day.
claims.quote: Triggers (per UTC calendar day) ... Custom indicators | 15,000 ... Limitations apply to each individual trigger type.

claims.claim: A record sharing a timestamp and UPN with another record in the same uploaded file is dropped.
claims.quote: If any record in the uploaded CSV file contains the same timestamp and UPN as other records in the file, the record is dropped.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft says to wait 24 hours after indicator and policy updates before uploading because immediate upload can leave data unscored.
claims.quote: Make sure to wait 24 hours before uploading the data after you update the custom indicators and the associated policies.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing: Licence; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Insider Risk Management requires a supported subscription and appropriate licences assigned to users, reported as per-user licensing.
claims.quote: To access and use Insider Risk Management, administrators need to verify their organization has a supported subscription and assign the appropriate licenses to users.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Licence; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a separate licence specific to custom indicators or the Insider Risk Indicators connector.
claims.quote: Searched: '"custom indicators" "license" "Insider" pricing' and 'Purview Insider Risk Management custom indicators connector licensing price default enabled'; read connector, policy indicators, Get started, billing models and the service-description licensing excerpt.

claims.claim: The billing models page meters the listed cloud storage, cloud service and Microsoft Fabric Insider Risk Management indicators in data security processing units.
claims.quote: Insider Risk Management indicators that detect activity in cloud storage apps (Box, Dropbox, Google Drive), cloud services (AWS, Azure), and Microsoft Fabric (Power BI) are billed on data security processing units.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Meter; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The billing models page does not list custom indicators, and no connector-specific charge or meter is published.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Purview Insider Risk Management custom indicators connector licensing price default enabled' and '"custom indicators" "license" "Insider" pricing'; read billing models, policy indicators, connector and Get started; found no custom-indicator meter or charge.

claims.claim: Microsoft suggests daily script scheduling with CSV refresh on a corresponding schedule.
claims.quote: schedule the script to run automatically on a recurring basis, such as once a day. This schedule requires updating the data in the CSV file on a similar (if not the same) schedule

claims.claim: Learn describes Insider Risk Management availability in tenants hosted in regions and countries supported by Azure service dependencies.
claims.quote: Insider Risk Management is currently available in tenants hosted in geographical regions and countries supported by Azure service dependencies.

claims.claim: The Insider Risk Management and Insider Risk Management Admins role groups can configure policies and settings.
claims.quote: Actions | Insider Risk Management | Insider Risk Management Admins ... Configure policies and settings | Yes | Yes

claims.claim: Creating the connector requires the separately assigned Data Connector Admin role.
claims.quote: Assign the Data Connector Admin role to the user who creates the connector in Step 3. This role is required to add connectors on the Data connectors page in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: Multiple role groups include the Data Connector Admin role by default.
claims.quote: Multiple role groups include this role by default.

claims.claim: Role-group membership is edited in Microsoft Purview portal through Settings > Roles and groups > Roles groups > Insider Risk Management > Edit > Choose users.
claims.quote: select Roles and groups, then select Roles groups in the left navigation pane. ... Select the Insider Risk Management role group, then select Edit. ... Select Choose users

claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember -Identity "Insider Risk Management" -Member "<user-UPN>" adds a user to that management role group.
claims.quote: Use the Add-RoleGroupMember cmdlet to add members to a management role group. ... The Identity parameter specifies the role group to add a member to. ... User ID or user principal name (UPN)

claims.claim: Connector creation begins in Microsoft Purview portal at Settings > Data connectors > My connectors > Add connector > Insider Risk Indicators (preview).
claims.quote: Select Settings > Data connectors. ... Select My connectors, then select Add connector. ... From the list, select Insider Risk Indicators (preview).

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no API or PowerShell operation to configure the Insider Risk Indicators connector; the upload script imports data instead.
claims.quote: Searched: 'site:learn.microsoft.com powershell "Insider Risk" "connector" create' and 'site:learn.microsoft.com/powershell "InsiderRisk" policy indicators connector New Set'; read connector setup and script sections; results document UI creation and data upload, not scripted configuration.

claims.claim: Custom indicator creation is reached in Microsoft Purview portal through Insider Risk Management > Settings > Policy indicators > Custom Indicators > Add custom indicator.
claims.quote: In Insider Risk Management settings, select Policy indicators and then select the Custom Indicators tab. ... Select Add custom indicator.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no API or PowerShell operation to configure these custom indicators.
claims.quote: Searched: 'site:learn.microsoft.com "custom indicators" "PowerShell" "policy"' and 'site:learn.microsoft.com "insider risk" "custom indicators" API create policy'; read policy-indicator custom-indicator steps and returned excerpts; no configuration API or cmdlet found.

claims.claim: Insider Risk Management > Policies in Microsoft Purview portal is the entry point for setting a policy's custom indicator and threshold.
claims.quote: Go to the Insider Risk Management solution. ... Select Policies in the left navigation. ... Select Create policy to open the policy workflow.
claims.fix: For the policy-indicator route, extend controls[3].ui.path to 'Insider Risk Management > Policies > Create policy > Policy template > Data theft or Data leaks template > Policy indicators > Decide whether to use default or custom indicator thresholds > Specify custom thresholds'. This is the route documented by https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/insider-risk-management-configure; keep the existing custom-trigger qualification in the note.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no API or PowerShell operation for selecting these custom indicators and thresholds in policies.
claims.quote: Searched: 'site:learn.microsoft.com "insider risk" "custom indicators" API create policy' and 'site:learn.microsoft.com/powershell "InsiderRisk" policy indicators connector New Set'; read Get started policy workflow and policy-indicator steps; found no matching configuration operation.

claims.claim: The policy workflow chooses the template on Policy template, indicators on Policy indicators, and custom thresholds through Specify custom thresholds; custom triggers are on the Triggers page for Data leaks templates.
claims.quote: On the Policy indicators page ... Select the indicators you want to apply to the policy. ... Choose either the Use default thresholds for all indicators or Specify custom thresholds

claims.claim: A Number field is required when configuring a custom indicator with a threshold.
claims.quote: Only fields that have a Number data type appear in the Data from mapping file list, since a Number data type is required to set a threshold value.

claims.claim: Connector setup maps the event time and Microsoft 365 user email fields.
claims.quote: Enter the values for Event time (UTC time) and Microsoft 365 user email address based on the appropriate values from the CSV file. These fields are mandatory for the connector.

claims.claim: The connector must exist before a custom indicator can be created, and the custom indicator must exist before it is selected in a policy.
claims.quote: To create a custom indicator to import third-party indicator data, you must first create an Insider Risk Indicators connector (preview). ... Now you can add the custom indicator to an insider risk policy

claims.claim: Custom-indicator triggers and insights appear in alerts, Activity explorer and User timeline.
claims.quote: After adding the custom indicator to your policies, the triggers and insights generated based on the custom indicators appear in the Alerts dashboard, Activity explorer, and User timeline.
